web_evidence.title: The Wedding People
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained authorized opening narrates Phoebe externally as she while directly presenting her perceptions, actions, and history.

web_evidence.title: A Q&A with Alison Espach, Author of August Indie Next List Top Pick “The Wedding People”
web_evidence.note: The interviewer identifies the novel as third person, and Espach explicitly explains choosing and modulating third person throughout this book to create intimacy with and distance from Phoebe.

person_note: The controlling narration is close third person, primarily focalized through Phoebe. Numerous extended quotes narrate Phoebe externally as she while rendering her memories, perceptions, and free-indirect thoughts. The authorized publisher opening independently shows the same structure, and Espach explicitly describes writing this book in third person and varying its distance from Phoebe. Scattered first-person quotations are clipped dialogue or local thought—several are explicitly attributed elsewhere in the quote set—and do not form sustained first-person sections. Generic you passages are aphorisms, not second-person narration. No credible evidence of alternating base persons was found.
